newsitem.title: USA: California governor undergoes minor throat surgery.
newsitem.headline: California governor undergoes minor throat surgery.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson underwent minor surgery on his throat Friday to strengthen his voice, his doctor said.

"Today's procedure was recommended to correct a persistent intermittent harshness in his vocal quality," Gerald Berke, who performed the operation, said. Berke said it went as planned and without complications.

The outpatient procedure, performed at the University of California at Los Angeles Medical Center, lasted 40 minutes and required a small incision on Wilson's neck under local anesthesia, Berke said. The doctor then removed a tiny plastic implant in his throat, which was placed there in July as part of a previous procedure.
His doctors said they found no evidence of abnormal tissue or cancer.

After the procedure Berke advised Wilson to rest his voice for several days. Wilson's office said the Republican governor would take several days' vacation and resume his normal work schedule Dec. 30.
Wilson spokesman Ron Low said the governor was resting comfortably at home. "We've spoken to the governor this evening. He's feeling fine. He's doing well," Low said.
Friday's minor surgery was a follow-up to two previous procedures to improve the quality of Wilson's croaky voice.
In April 1995 Wilson had a small benign nodule in his throat removed. In July 1996 the governor underwent a minor procedure that brought his vocal cords closer together to strengthen his voice.
